evidence.quote: | true, days when days > 0 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule is in Tier 1 (Summa.Ledger dueDate). The wording is in Tier 1 (termsText, termsWords). Parsing the form value is in Tier 2 (Summa.Web.Engine) and the codec is in Tier 2 (Summa.Storage). The change adds nothing to Tier 3 or Tier 4.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no clock, randomness, I/O or persistence call. dueDate and the parser are pure functions, and the storage codec only maps values to and from JSON.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The wording "Net {days} EOM" is written twice, in termsText and in the audit termsWords. This copies the existing duplication of "Net {days}". The 1 to 365 limit is a literal repeated in the parser branches. The copies agree, so I scored 1.

evidence.quote:
| DayOfNextMonth day ->
 let nextMonth = DateOnly(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month, 1).AddMonths 1

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule and the ordinal wording are in Tier 1. The form parsing and the 1 to 28 day check are in Tier 2 (Engine and Storage). Tier 3 and Tier 4 only call these.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds only pure code: dueDate, ordinalDay, the parser and the codec. It adds no effect and bypasses no port.

evidence.quote: if day >= 1 && day <= 28 then Ok(DayOfNextMonth day)
| true, day when day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))
| DayOfNextMonth day -> $"Due the {ordinalDay day} of next month"
| Some(DayOfNextMonth day) -> $"Due the {ordinalDay day} of next month"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: ordinalDay is defined once and used in both places, which is good. The 1 to 28 range is a literal in both the storage decoder and the engine parser, with no shared constant or predicate in Ledger. The phrase "Due the … of next month" is also written in both termsText and termsWords. All copies agree, so I scored 1.
